sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Plantation, FL?
sections.html:
Yes. A Plantation homeowner can accept a cash offer and close once title work is done, or list the house and wait for a financed buyer. The city sits in the middle of Broward County, directly west of Fort Lauderdale, so most buyers weigh commute, schools and flood risk as much as the house itself.

The city's demographics page lists a 2018 population of 94,288 and an area of 22.8 square miles. It describes the housing as single and multi-family dwellings with values from $125,000 to over $2 million, and a median value of $271,200 at the time of that count. Those numbers are dated, so treat them as background and ask a local agent or the Broward County Property Appraiser for current values.

  • A cash buyer closes on your schedule and takes the house as it is.
  • A listed sale suits a house in showing condition with no title problems.
  • A house with liens, tenants or an open estate needs clearing in either case.

sections.h2: Where did Plantation come from, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Plantation was planned. Frederick Peters moved to South Florida in 1931 and bought 10,000 acres along State Road 7, and he hired architect Russell Pancoast to write a master plan. That plan included an ordinance against neighboring homes looking alike, minimum lot sizes and separate residential, commercial and industrial zones.

The city was incorporated on April 30, 1953, with fewer than 500 residents and a budget of $1,288. The first council meeting took place in an old feed warehouse on May 11, 1953. Growth in the 1970s through the 1990s pushed boundaries west to Flamingo Road, so the city's western neighborhoods are newer than the original Plantation Acres and historic district areas near Fig Tree Lane and Palm Tree Road.

Lot size and zoning rules from the master-plan era still shape what a buyer can build or add. Ask the city's building department about permitted additions before you quote a buyer any rebuilding plan.

sections.h2: What is the Plantation economy and climate like?
sections.html:
The city lists education services, healthcare, finance and insurance, retail, entertainment and food services as leading industries, with more than 5,000 registered businesses and over 47,000 people employed. It names Motorola Solutions, National Beverage and Magic Leap as large firms in its About page, and its history page adds Florida Power and Light, DHL, Westside Regional Medical Center and Plantation General Hospital.

The climate is subtropical, with average rainfall of 62 inches, an average temperature of 75.4 degrees, a winter mean of 66.5 and a summer mean of 84.2. That rain and heat shape what inspectors and insurers look at in a house: roofs, windows, drainage and air conditioning. A buyer's insurance quote can affect whether a financed deal survives, which is one reason cash offers appeal here.

Schools listed by the city include six public elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools, plus 32 private schools. Transportation includes I-95, I-595 and I-75 access, Tri-Rail, Amtrak and Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport.

sections.h2: What do Plantation sellers pay at closing?
sections.html:
The main state tax is documentary stamp tax on the deed, set at 70 cents per $100 of consideration. The Department of Revenue says Broward County uses the standard rate, which differs from Miami-Dade, where the rate is 60 cents plus a surtax with an exception for single-family homes. Consideration includes any mortgage on the property.

Recording charges are set in section 28.24. The first page is $5.00 and each added page is $4.00, plus $1.00 for each name beyond four and per-page trust fund and technology charges. Every party to the deed is liable for the stamp tax under Department of Revenue guidance, so the contract should say who pays.

sections.h2: How does Broward County property tax affect a Plantation sale?
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1 and tax bills go out in November. The state's discount schedule runs 4 percent for November payment, then 3, 2 and 1 percent for the following three months, and delinquency begins April 1. The city's history page says Plantation has one of the lowest millage rates in Broward County; ask the county for the current rate on your address.

A homestead exemption of up to $50,000 requires an application by March 1. Save Our Homes caps yearly assessment growth at the lower of 3 percent or CPI, and the state's chart shows a 2.7 percent cap for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025. A sale resets value, so a buyer's bill can rise sharply. A seller moving to another Florida homestead can apply the portability benefit within three years.

  • Non-homestead assessed value can rise no more than 10 percent a year.
  • Disabled veterans and seniors may qualify for added reductions through county or city ordinance.
  • Appeals of value go to the value adjustment board within 25 days of the August notice.

sections.h2: What if my Plantation house has a foreclosure, an estate or a tenant?
sections.html:
You still have options. A foreclosure judgment leads to a clerk's sale 20 to 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to extend, and the high bidder pays a 5 percent deposit. A private sale before then can settle the loan.

For an inherited house, summary administration covers estates up to $150,000 or deaths more than two years ago. Creditor claim deadlines come from section 733.702, and Florida has no estate tax for deaths after 2004. For a rented house, the landlord gives a three-day notice for unpaid rent excluding weekends and holidays, a seven-day notice for a curable violation, and 30 days for a month-to-month ending. Because this involves court steps, confirm your facts with a Florida attorney.

sections.h2: What steps does a Plantation cash sale follow?
sections.html:
Expect five stages from first call to funds.

  1. Share the address, condition, loan balance and occupancy.
  2. Review the written offer and confirm the closing date and who pays each fee.
  3. Title work finds liens and open taxes.
  4. You sign the deed before two witnesses.
  5. The Broward County clerk records it and collects stamp tax, and your proceeds are paid.

Keep your recorded deed and settlement statement for future tax filings.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax the same in Broward as in Miami-Dade?
faqs.a: No. Broward uses 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Miami-Dade uses 60 cents plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, which the Department of Revenue says does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property resets to just value on the next January 1. You may be able to carry savings to a new Florida homestead through portability.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to sell a Plantation house?
faqs.a: Not for every sale, but a title company or attorney handles the deed, lien search and closing. Use an attorney for probate, foreclosure or a disputed occupant.
